title: Streamlit log handler
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

A streamlit log handler to allow using Streamlit to show logs.

### Why?

Python's built-in logging framework is extremely versatile. Hooking into that would make debugging easier.

In my own app, I have observations I both want to save to a log system and show to the user. Having a streamlit log handler allows me to do that without duplicating code.

### How?

I have written something that I use in my own project that can be used as a starting place:

```
import logging

import streamlit as st


class StreamlitLogHandler(logging.Handler):
    """
    Log handler to display logs in Streamlit app.

    This handler formats log messages and sends them to the Streamlit app for display.
    If the log record contains an "object" attribute, its value will be displayed in an expander.
    If the log record contains a "link" attribute, the log text will be a link with the content as the target address.

    If streamlit session state contains a "log_container", logs will be displayed there.
    Otherwise, logs will be displayed on the page as they are emitted.
    """

    [USER]
    def get_icon(levelno: int) -> str:
        if levelno <= logging.INFO:
            return "ℹ️"
        elif levelno <= logging.WARNING:
            return "⚠️"
        elif levelno <= logging.ERROR:
            return "❌"
        else:
            return "🛑"

    def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord):
        if "log_container" in st.session_state and isinstance(
            st.session_state["log_container"], st.delta_generator.DeltaGenerator
        ):
            log_container = st.session_state["log_container"]
        else:
            log_container = st
        msg = self.format(record)
        if "link" in record.__dict__:
            msg = f"[{msg}]({record.__dict__['link']})"
        if "object" in record.__dict__:
            with log_container.expander(
                msg, expanded=False, icon=self.get_icon(record.levelno)
            ):
                log_container.write(record.__dict__["object"])
        else:
            if record.levelno <= logging.INFO:
                log_container.info(msg)
            elif record.levelno <= logging.WARNING:
                log_container.warning(msg)
            else:
                log_container.error(msg)

```

The "log_containter" in st.session_state allows you to specify where the logs should be shown. The obvious use case is a collapsed expander that can be opened to see what logs there are. It is not the most transparent way of doing it, and it risks them not being shown (if it is set on on page, and the page is then changed).

You can set the object to show by e.g. `logger.error("Example error log message", extra={"object": object_to_log})`

You can set where you want the text to link to by e.g `logger.error("Example error log message.",extra={"link": "#" + self.name})`. This allows you to link in the same page (used as shown) or another page. You could also make the log message into a markdown text with the link, but you typically don't want that in other log systems, so doing that would make the logging less versatile.

This is just a suggestion, it works for my app, but I am sure many improvements can be done.
